title: Genetics of congenital heart disease and the work-up after diagnosis

items.question: Why is the rate of chromosomal abnormality higher in fetuses with heart disease than in infants?
options: Affected fetuses more often die before birth
Heart disease causes aneuploidy after birth
items.explanation: Fetal series show 30-40% abnormal karyotypes, more than infants, probably because of higher mortality in utero.

items.question: According to series summarised in AHA 2014, what chromosomal-abnormality rate was reported when fetal heart disease appeared isolated on ultrasound?
options: Zero, if the defect is isolated
items.explanation: The AHA 2014 statement reported a risk of at least 15-30% in historical series of apparently isolated fetal heart disease; this is not a current case-specific prediction.

items.question: Atrioventricular septal defect with normal situs. What proportion have trisomy 21?
items.explanation: 50-70% of fetuses with AVSD and normal situs have trisomy 21.

items.question: D-transposition is diagnosed. The aneuploidy risk is very low. Should testing still be offered?
options: Yes: parents should still be offered testing
No: testing is never indicated in transposition
Only if the mother is over 35
items.explanation: These lesions are rarely aneuploid, but testing should still be offered. Genetic testing and counselling should be recommended for every fetus with a cardiac malformation.

items.question: Of these options, which lesion had the highest reported 22q11 deletion frequency in AHA 2014 Table 11?
items.explanation: AHA 2014 Table 11 gives 50-90% for interrupted aortic arch.

items.question: A cardiac tumour is seen at 26 weeks. What should it prompt?
options: Genetic testing: over 60% have tuberous sclerosis
items.explanation: A tumour in mid or late gestation should prompt genetic testing; over 60% have tuberous sclerosis.

items.question: Before microarray testing, what must parents be told?
options: It may find variants of unknown significance
items.explanation: Variants of unknown significance should be disclosed before testing; microarray cannot detect balanced rearrangements.

items.question: After a cardiac diagnosis, what survey of the rest of the fetus is recommended?
options: A detailed survey of all anatomy by an expert, repeated later if appropriate
None; the heart is the only concern
items.explanation: A detailed expert survey is recommended for every fetus with heart disease; some anomalies only appear later.
